item.title: Agents Aren't the Point. State Is.
item.description: Agentic AI obsesses over the agent — the model, the harness, the loop. The thing that actually has to survive from start to finish is the state of the work. LangGraph knew this early. Claude Code and Codex prove it by accident.

item.title: How an Idea Grows Up
item.description: The transformer is a 2017 paper. Claude Code is 2026. That's nine years for one idea to grow up — and almost none of it was the idea getting better. A rule for how a breakthrough matures into real impact: four gaps, two rules, then run forward onto quantum computing.

item.title: Interesting Things I Found — July 2026
item.description: Fourteen open-source projects, two months on — from the model runtime up to a finished application. The theme isn't new capability; it's learning to operate the agent stack we already have.

item.title: Start at the Cheap End
item.description: Your agent costs too much or does too little, and there are about a dozen ways to fix that. They are not equal in effort. If you want a better agent by tonight, fine-tuning is the worst place to start, not the first.

item.title: How to build a knowledge base
item.description: Storage is not knowledge. On the inference layer a real knowledge base needs, where to put it, how to assemble knowledge like packages, and how to grade it.

item.title: The Seat Needs a Watcher
item.description: The single seat from my last post isn't owned, it's won — moment to moment, by whatever signal is loudest. Meditation trains a watcher for that inside your head. A long-context agent needs one built outside it.

item.title: Trending Tools to Watch — May 2026
item.description: A tour through twelve open-source projects shaping how we build, route, and remember work with AI agents.

item.title: What Comes After the Transformer?
item.description: The cost of scaling is exploding while the gains shrink. A tour of the three escape routes — MoE, world models, and Google's memory-and-sleep line — then a closer look at the five ways people are trying to make a frozen model keep learning.

item.title: Why model hallucinate?
item.description: Some explaination about why model hallucinate

item.title: Give Your AI Agent a Personality
item.description: Three files, three mechanisms — how CLAUDE.md, Skills, and Hooks work together to give an AI agent a stable, consistent identity.

item.title: Words We Code By
item.description: Five common engineering words — testable, lean, DRY, symbolic, abstraction — and the bigger ideas they smuggle past the surface.

item.title: You can't fork yourself
item.description: The brain isn't sequential — it's parallel hardware with one serial seat. Why focus is a count, not a skill, and how to work with agents that can fork when you can't.
